inputs.original_text: South Portland’s schools are facing another major budget shortfall, with more than 70 positions set to be cut. Families and taxpayers deserve more than apologies: they deserve to know how the district got here and why classroom needs weren’t protected. Schools should put students, parents, and basic education first—not let administrative priorities crowd out the people doing the work. It’s time for honest accounting, disciplined spending, and real accountability.
inputs.modified_text: South Portland’s schools are preparing to cut more than 70 positions, and families deserve a plain accounting—not another round of excuses. A school system’s first duty is to educate children and support the people who teach them, not protect administrative priorities. Taxpayers have a right to know how this happened and who is accountable. Careful stewardship, clear priorities, and respect for families should come before bureaucratic comfort.
